hldContextSlice.frameworkSummary:
Three records carry the design, and both paths into the analyzer use them: the lookup pipeline that serves the agent tools and builds every run context, and the plan tree above it that serves broad analyses. The plan tree does not run today for a request that asks no specific question, so two Stories first make such a request run and then make a broad analysis complete; the other Stories apply to both paths once it does. A completeness record on every lookup result and every plan-task result replaces today's mix of truncated flags, totals, free-text notes and log lines: it says whether the result is complete, how many items exist and were returned, why any are missing, what was skipped or only partly read, and what the result rests on (text on disk, the stored graph, the document index, a live data source). A lookup that cannot run is always the existing failed output with its reason, never an empty result, and a failure to write the answer is reported with what was found, not passed silently to another way of answering. An answer report heads every answer on both paths: one overall completeness statement derived from those records, the measured size, and how the request was handled.

A request measure says what a request touches and maps it to the existing five sizes. It has two sources, because the size is needed at two different moments. A request that plans lookups up front is measured from what those lookups returned. A request that plans none up front (an unfocused request on the plan-tree path, where the size is needed before planning) is measured from the area it names: the files and entities the graph store holds under the path or repo it points at. No size is taken from the wording or assumed; a request that cannot be measured is treated as the largest size and says so.

Handling is a stated table from size to method, on both paths. Up to the size a model can reason over together, the answer is written in one pass, as today. Above it, the results are divided into parts along file and directory boundaries, each part is reasoned over in turn, and a combine step joins the per-part results into one answer; a failed part is kept out and named in the report. A single item too large for one pass is read in consecutive sections under the same rule. Once that handling exists the limits are removed: no lookup, plan-task runtime, planning prompt or text search keeps a limit on how many results it returns or how much of an item it reads. Last, layouts are selected by question kind and source kind together; a new question kind, enumeration, is rendered directly from lookup results with no model in the path, and the layouts lose their limits and describe every lookup they may draw on.

ownedContracts.name: Handling report
ownedContracts.purpose: How a request was handled: at once or in parts, how many parts, and which parts were not covered.

consumedContracts.name: Completeness record
consumedContracts.purpose: The one statement every lookup result and every plan-task result carries about whether it is complete; also the rule that a lookup which cannot run is the failed output, never an empty result. The existing failed output is kept for a lookup that could not run, and gains one optional field for what was found before it failed.

consumedContracts.name: Answer report
consumedContracts.purpose: The header every answer carries on both paths: overall completeness derived from the results, then the measured size and how the request was handled once those exist. Owned by the first Story so that sizing, handling and layout each fill and render their part.

consumedContracts.name: Request measure
consumedContracts.purpose: What a request actually touched, from its lookup results or from the area it names, and the size it maps to.

consumedContracts.name: Causes of not proceeding
consumedContracts.purpose: What a request that cannot proceed reports. Three codes are added, all declared by Story s6, to the plan tree's existing list (RunErrorCode) and to the daemon's error codes (AnalyzeRpcErrorCode); its failure type (RunFailure) and its stages (RunStage) are kept as they are, and 'shaper-llm-unavailable' is kept for a model call that failed. A kind of scope that does not go with a kind of source keeps the existing code 'scope-ref-kind-target-mismatch'.

boundary.internal: The table from size to handling method and the size above which results are handled in parts. How outputs are divided along directory and file boundaries, and one large item into consecutive sections, so that a single item is read in full. In the lookup pipeline: writing a per-part result for each part serially and the new combine step (its input, its output, its own size rule, its failure case). On the plan tree: the same size rule on the aggregator's input, combining in stages. Keeping a failed part out of the combined answer. The step tool's part turn. Filling the handling report and showing it in the answer. The limits are still in place, so this is exercised by results that are large within them and by tests that lower the threshold. This Story closes the exception accepted on Story s7: a broad docs analysis whose aggregate input is larger than one model call accepts must complete once that input is handled in parts.

adjacentBoundaries.internal: With every limit still in place: returning the completeness record from each lookup and each plan-task runtime, saying when a limit was reached (limited), what was skipped and what was only partly read, and the basis each rests on. For the text search, reporting what it leaves out today: files over its size limit, files it could not read, lines it shortened, output it discarded, and the files each backend excludes by rule. Classifying every catch clause in the lookups and the plan-task runtimes: a clause that handles a named, expected condition stays and names what it skipped in the record; a clause that swallows an error is removed or rethrows, so that the lookup becomes the failed output. Deriving the answer report's overall completeness from those records and writing the completeness line at the head of every answer on both paths, in the layouts as they are today. Reporting a failure of the answer-writing step as a typed error that carries the lookup results and the report, in place of the 'model unavailable' error that discards them today, added as one more case to the raise site and the mapping that Story s6 owns, and passed through everything that reaches the context builder (six callers, the one-shot agent tool and the daemon's workflow runner, with the error's data carried through the daemon's error mapping). Keeping the report out of the schema given to a model at both places the schema reaches one (the answer-writing call and the tool loop's final answer), and rejecting a report an agent supplies. What the step tool attaches to a bundle the agent wrote. The declared report field on the bundle, its schema version, and how bundles and run records stored before the change are treated. The lookup cache's version. The lookup cache's stored shape changes with the outputs. The free-form fallback: an optional field for partial findings on the failed output, the loop's exit at the limit attaching what it gathered, reaching its turn limit becoming a failed output, and its answer gets a report that says it rests on a search directed by a model. Reading the data drivers' cut flag into the completeness record of the table-listing lookup and the object-listing plan task.

The two measuring sources and the mapping from counts to the five sizes. From lookup results, at all four places that assume a size today. From the named area, on the plan tree: the measuring pass after both classification branches, removal of the scope picker's model call, removal of the size from the classifier's output, what the decomposer and planner receive as size at each moment, the size's effect on plan depth as well as task count, and measuring a child plan from the area it names when it is spawned, with the planner model's figure and a size on the daemon request kept as hints. A size given by a caller or a slash command kept as a hint. The unmeasurable case. Filling the measure into the answer report and showing it in the answer. The source of the measure for each of the seven kinds of scope, including counting a data connection's tables or objects from the live source through the data driver, and the fallback to XL, recorded as not determined, when a count cannot be taken. Adding a complete mode to the data drivers' listings for the count (the five relational drivers, four of the six namespace drivers, the file listing; Redis and etcd are recorded as not determined, since their listing is a sample of keys), with the limited mode kept for other callers; a listing that reports it was cut is never a determined count.

Removing every limit on how many results a lookup or plan-task runtime returns: the sixteen sites the Define lists and those found since, in the lookups (the maxSources parameter of the two document lookups, the result cut in document retrieval, the cuts inside capability reuse-check, table describe and the document family summary, the preview limits of doc.mention) and in the plan-task runtimes (the file-list and file caps of data and infrastructure discovery and their sample caps). Removing the fixed cuts on an item's content at nine sites: the eight found when the Epic was defined, including the three adherence checks, and the indexer's own cut of a stored body to 8,192 characters (src/indexer/parser/artifact.ts), which Story s1 reports with the item's real length. The index is a pointer: at each of the nine sites, where an item's content matters to the answer, the analyzer reads the item from its file at the place the index points to and does not rely on the body the index stores. What the index stores and how it is built are not changed. The complete mode of the text search for both backends: no limit on hits, no per-file match limit, no cut of a matching line, no skipping of a file for its size, no discarding of output (the search's output is read as a stream, not kept up to a fixed size), a stated rule for a search that runs out of time (reported as failed, never as complete), and the files each backend excludes by rule stated in the result. Removing the limit parameters, their examples and the fan-out bound from the planning prompt. What was reported as limited in Story s1 now does not occur; the larger results are handled by Story s3's method. Raising the lookup cache's version again, and dropping limit parameters before a lookup's cache key is taken. Building cancellation (a signal from each caller through the context builder to a check between turns; the run's signal into the plan walk and the classifier; the optional signal on the daemon's standard handlers; the signal parameter on the daemon's context-building functions; a signal on the step tool's plan and narrow phases, through stepPlan and the runner context; the new cancel request for the five requests received over the socket that reach a tool loop (the three context requests, the plan request and the classify request), with the daemon's table of run id to canceller; the cancelled case in the classify stage's mapping; 'aborted' in the daemon's error codes; what a cancelled loop returns), moving the table-listing lookup and the object-listing plan task to the complete mode of the data drivers' listings, and only then removing the turn limit and retiring its configuration setting (catalog row, retired list, the analyzer's configuration, the planning prompt, the VS Code extension's declaration with a release, the pages that document it, the reconcile fixture) for all three users of the loop (the free-form lookup and the classification and task modes) and giving the loop the complete mode of its search tools. Removing the error and the code for reaching the turn limit from both lists and both mappings, with the tests that import the error and the test configuration that sets the limit.

Adding the enumeration question kind to the planner's choices and rendering it directly from lookup results, including returning it from the step tool's plan phase with no model turn. Choosing a layout by question kind and source kind at both places a layout is selected today. Removing the limits from the six layouts and the older per-source layouts and from the summariser's output schema. Making each layout describe every lookup it may draw on, with that reference at the end of the prompt. Laying out the answer report, which Stories s1 to s3 already write, in the form each layout uses.

Giving a request that asks no specific question a run context: what the lookup pipeline plans for it (a broad survey of the area it names, from the lookups that exist) where today it returns at once; the same for a request started with a stated kind of source, which is always marked unfocused; serving, in the lookup pipeline, the four kinds of scope it returns for today (a file, a symbol, a manifest directory, a data connection), and how each resolves to what the lookups need. Replacing the single 'model unavailable' error with the cause of each way of not proceeding, as new codes in the existing list and new typed errors, and with the existing codes where one fits: every place the pipeline returns nothing, and the fall-through for a bundle that fails validation, is listed and given its cause. It owns the place the error is raised, the pipeline's rule for returning nothing, and the functions that map these errors to codes (the plan tree's and the daemon's, and the classify stage's mapping, through which an error from the classifier's context build is routed). The form of a symbol scope's value, its resolution to one stored entity, and the validator and classifier prompt brought in line. The one function that resolves a scope's value to a repo, a path or an entity, and moving the lookup pipeline's direct readers of the value to it (the planning prompt, the context builder's path resolution, the indexed check). Correcting the table of which kind of scope goes with which kind of source, with the classifier prompt's copy of it, the table's comment and the matrix test, and applying it on both classification branches: the plan tree's classify mapping surfaces the validator's inner code, and the branch with no classifier calls the validator's checks directly. Supplying the connection check from both callers of the classifier, and mapping a connection id to its repo. It declares all three new codes in both lists; Stories s1 and s7 raise one each.

Widening the plan tasks of each family (code, docs, infra, data) to exactly the kinds of scope the corrected table gives it, with the scope check the docs tasks share with the code tasks taking the family's row as an argument, and every task that reads the scope's value directly (three docs tasks, the shared adherence task, the task that lists data connections) moved to the resolution function Story s6 defines, including a data connection for the data tasks, and refusing any other pairing with the existing code for it. Running a broad analysis through classification, the run context, planning, the plan walk with its nested plans, and the aggregator, to a final report; finding and correcting what stops it at each stage. A stop the run catches is already recorded; what is added is a handler for an error nothing catches, in the plan walk and in the daemon's request, that writes the run record, and the rule that a record still in progress with no live run behind it is abandoned: the process's in-memory count of the runs it is executing per id, and the two readers that apply it, the status request and the purge, each rewriting the record as failed with the code 'run-abandoned', which Story s6 declares and this Story raises; a new run replaces a record left in progress with its own first record. Making a task's refusal of a scope a typed error the plan walk recognises, with an optional code on the failed-task record. Its design begins by running one and recording how far it gets; if what is found is more than one Story, it is brought back to be split. Two stops the first runs of 2026-10-08 found are corrected here as well: the aggregate-report task runs on the inputs that exist when a task before it failed and is told which are absent, so that a run with a failed task returns a report that names what is missing; and the daemon's run request accepts an empty prompt when the caller states the kind of source. Two further stops are not this Story's: what the code tasks treat as a module is Story s8's, and an aggregate input larger than one model call accepts is Story s3's. For the second, a broad docs analysis not completing on a repository of that size is an exception the stakeholder accepted on 2026-10-08, to be closed by Story s3.
Private implementation of s8: The code tasks of a broad analysis work on a repository whose graph has no modules for its directories

nonFunctional.performance: A request small enough for one pass makes the same model calls as today, and one fewer on the plan tree, where the model call that picked a size is replaced by a count from the graph store. A request handled in parts makes one call per part plus the combination, serially; that time is accepted because accuracy comes before cost. After the limits are removed, a complete text search over a large repository is the cost of a text lookup.
nonFunctional.observability: Every answer on both paths states its completeness, its measured size and counts, and its handling method and part count; each lookup and plan-task result states its own completeness. A failed lookup, part or answer-writing step carries its reason.
nonFunctional.durability: Cached lookup outputs written before this change lack the completeness record and are treated as absent, not as complete.
nonFunctional.security: No change: lookups stay inside the repository's dependency closure and the existing scope checks on paths remain.

summary.prose: This Story adds one shared helper that divides an answer-writing model call's input into ordered parts when either the HLD's table from measured size to method says the request is above the partition size, or the rendered input does not fit a conservative character budget measured before every provider attempt. Each part is reasoned over serially, evidence and findings are assembled in code, and a staged combine writes only a bounded summary and always ends. Four callers use it: the lookup synthesis, the free-form lookup's final emit, the plan-tree aggregator and the step tool's answer turn. The handling report is typed, carried to the delivered answer on every path (including the free-form short-circuit and the plan tree's aggregates), shown in the answer's head, and a failed part, a failed combine or a failure that carries data is reported without losing the other results.

returns.meaning: The bundle: the one call made today when the size is below the partition size and the input fits, else the assembled bundle of the parts.

errors.condition: The fixed context leaves no room for the minimum section, a combine stage cannot shrink, or every part failed; carries the lookup results and the report.
Existing: no prompt for the key.

A failed combine returns the per-part results with the failure reported, it does not throw

dataModelChanges.details: The sc4 contract typed. method, parts, partitionedBy, notCovered[{part, reason}] as sketched, plus additive fields: combineStages (optional), inputChars, budgetChars, budgetSource ('provider' | 'context-window' | 'default'), and trigger ('size' | 'fit' | 'both') saying which condition divided it. partitionedBy gains 'mixed'. Counting: parts is the number of first-level parts including failed ones; a single pass has parts 1. A part id is its ordinal and heading ('part 3: docs/a'); mergeHandling qualifies it with the plan path. Composition by mergeHandling(first, second, prefix): an absent side is ignored; method is 'partitioned' if either is; parts is the sum of the two parts counts (a single pass counts 1); notCovered is the concatenation with the first side's part ids qualified by the prefix; inputChars is the maximum; budgetChars and budgetSource are those of the side with the smaller budgetChars; combineStages is the sum when either has it; partitionedBy is the common value or 'mixed'; trigger is the union. So a single-pass root with a partitioned child reports 'partitioned' with parts one more than the child's.
dataModelChanges.schemaDiff: readonly combineStages?: number | undefined; readonly inputChars: number; readonly budgetChars: number; readonly budgetSource: 'provider' | 'context-window' | 'default'; readonly trigger: 'size' | 'fit' | 'both'; partitionedBy adds 'mixed'

dataModelChanges.details: Type changes from unknown to HandlingReport | undefined. Current-behaviour invariant it might break: the bundle schema declares handling as an open object, so a stored value such as {} is valid today, and isAnswerReport does not validate it. A read-boundary guard parseHandling(value: unknown): HandlingReport | undefined accepts only a value with the required fields and treats anything else as absent; mergeHandling, renderReportHead and isAnswerReport use it, and a stored {} is read as no handling.

HANDLING_TABLE maps the sc3 size to the method: XS and S single pass, M, L and XL partitioned; 'determined: false' is XL, so an unmeasured request is partitioned. answerInputBudget(provider?, outputTokens?) returns {chars, source}: provider.inputBudgetChars when declared (source 'provider'); else for a local model (window tokens minus outputTokens) times 2 characters per token (source 'context-window'), where the window is the figure ollamaContextWindow gives num_ctx; else 60,000 characters (source 'default', also used by the step tool, which has no provider); a 16,000-character reserve is then subtracted for framing, schema text and the first repair note. The decision to divide is: the table says partitioned, OR the rendered input (messages, repeated context, absent-input section) exceeds the budget. The fit is measured before every provider attempt, including each repair retry with the actual repair note, which is capped at 8,000 characters of listed errors (the rest summarised as a count); a retry that would not fit divides the part further, up to three times. The ratio is a conservative estimate and not a bound: no character count can prove a local model's input fits, completeStructured returns parsed content only and Ollama's processed-token count is cache-dependent and not returned, so the report records the budget and its source and does not claim truncation is prevented.

dataModelChanges.entity: PartPlan, PartResult and the caller adapters
dataModelChanges.details: A PartPlan is the ordered blocks of the evidence with an ordinal separate from the block key, grouped by directory then file in stable order; one block larger than the room is cut into consecutive sections of at least 4,000 characters, each keeping its key and an index. A PartResult holds the part's heading, its summary (capped at 2,000 characters by the schema) and its assembled content. The bundle adapter takes system, focus and summary from the final combine and concatenates structure, surface, artefacts and upstream of the covered parts by ordinal under part headings; the aggregate adapter takes the summary from the final combine and concatenates the findings of the covered parts by ordinal, each keeping its sources. A combine reply is never read for evidence or findings. Combine stages: N summaries become ceil(N/g) with g at least 2, so it ends in at most ceil(log2 N) stages; if fixed context plus two capped summaries does not fit, HandlingBudgetError is raised. A combine failure returns the adapter's output from the per-part results with 'combine' in notCovered.

HandlingBudgetError is a typed error for a fixed context with no room for the minimum section, a stage that cannot shrink, or every part failed; it carries the lookup results and the report with every part named in notCovered. LookupFailedError (message, partial, cause) gains an optional handling field. The free-form lookup catches a HandlingBudgetError from the tool loop and throws a LookupFailedError carrying the tool results as partial and the handling, so executePlan keeps them in the failed output instead of dropping them, and the pipeline then raises the answer-step failure that Story s1 declares, with the report. The driver passes HandlingBudgetError through unchanged instead of mapping it to 'answer-invalid'.

AnswerProgress is {completed: PartResult[] by ordinal, pending: {kind 'part' | 'combine', ordinal or stage and group index}, stageOutputs, failures: {part, reason}[], retries}. It is held in the step state beside the stages awaiting_part and awaiting_combine and passed to prepareSynthesize and finalizeSynthesize(raw, execution, progress); the bundle handler persists it by re-encoding the state token on every valid transition, increments retries and re-encodes on an invalid reply, records the part or the combine as failed at the retry bound and continues, and releases it on terminal success and failure. The handler consumes FinalizedAnswerTurn: 'final' continues as today with the layers and records the handling; 'next' persists the progress and emits the next turn. A state written before the change lacks progress and is read as a single-pass state.

Two outputs added to the StepOutput union beside StepOutputEmitBundle with the same fields plus the part ordinal and total, or the stage and group. A reply reuses the registered bundle argument of seven string layers (a part reply is a seven-layer bundle of that part with its summary within the cap; a combine reply fills system, focus and summary and leaves the four evidence layers empty), so the registered MCP schema and StepInputBundle are unchanged and the legacy emit_bundle turn is kept. A typed answer failure is returned as StepOutputError with the code Story s1 declares and its data, not as an uncaught exception.

Carries the HandlingReport of the aggregator call, validated by parseHandling on read. collectPlanSources reads it for the aggregate task of the root plan and of each nested plan, and concludeRun merges them with the run context's handling through mergeHandling, so uncovered parts make the run's completeness false.

interactionWithShared.howDetails: Types HandlingReport with additive fields (combineStages, inputChars, budgetChars, budgetSource, trigger, and 'mixed' for partitionedBy), states the composition rules, and fills it on every answer of both paths.
Fills AnswerReport.handling; keeps the binary mergeAnswerReports(first, second, prefix); renders one handling line in renderReportHead; uncovered parts add source notes and make completeness false.
A result whose part or combine failed is incomplete; plan-task completeness records are read as today and the aggregate's handling is added as sources.
Reads RequestMeasure.size for HANDLING_TABLE (an undetermined measure is XL); measure.characters stays a hint.
Uses the answer-step-failed code declared by sc6 and raised by Story s1 for HandlingBudgetError and all-parts-failed; no new code.

errorCases.scenario: A part's model call fails, or its reply fails the schema after the bounded retries
errorCases.detection: The part call throws, or finalizeSynthesize raises SynthesizerSchemaUnrecoverable and progress.retries reaches the structured-output retry setting
errorCases.response: The part is recorded in failures and named in HandlingReport.notCovered with its qualified id and reason; the other parts are kept; completeness is false
errorCases.userImpact: The answer is delivered and names the part that was not covered and why

errorCases.detection: failures holds all parts and completed is empty
errorCases.response: HandlingBudgetError is raised with the lookup results and the report, and is returned as the answer-step failure that Story s1 declares
errorCases.userImpact: A typed failure that keeps what the lookups found; no empty answer is written

errorCases.scenario: The combine call fails or its reply stays invalid after the retries
errorCases.detection: The combine call throws, or its reply fails the schema at the retry bound
errorCases.response: The output is built from the per-part results unchanged by the adapter, its summary layer being the part summaries concatenated by ordinal, and 'combine' is added to notCovered; nothing is thrown
errorCases.userImpact: The per-part results are returned with the combine failure reported

errorCases.scenario: A combine stage cannot shrink its input
errorCases.detection: The helper checks before a stage that fixed context plus two capped summaries fits the budget, and after a stage that the count of summaries fell
errorCases.response: If the check before fails, HandlingBudgetError is raised; if the count did not fall, the stage is treated as a combine failure and the per-part fallback applies

errorCases.scenario: The fixed context alone, or one minimum section with it, exceeds the budget
errorCases.detection: Fixed rendered characters plus the minimum section of 4,000 characters is more than the budget
errorCases.response: HandlingBudgetError with the results and the report; dividing the evidence cannot make the call fit, so no partial answer is written
errorCases.userImpact: A typed failure that says the context is larger than the model accepts

errorCases.scenario: A schema-repair retry would not fit
errorCases.detection: The helper measures the actual input of the retry (the part, the schema text and the repair note, which lists every validation error and is capped at 8,000 characters with the rest counted) before the attempt
errorCases.response: The part is divided into smaller consecutive sections up to three times, then recorded as not covered
errorCases.userImpact: A malformed reply with many errors cannot push a call over the limit unnoticed

errorCases.scenario: The provider refuses a part as too large
errorCases.detection: InputTooLargeError from the provider, whose sizes may be undefined
errorCases.response: The part is divided into smaller consecutive sections up to three times, and then recorded as not covered
errorCases.userImpact: The part is read in full or named; nothing is silently cut

errorCases.scenario: A local model's input is larger than the estimate said
errorCases.detection: Not detectable by the caller: completeStructured returns parsed content only and Ollama's processed-token count is cache-dependent and not returned
errorCases.response: Not claimed to be prevented: the estimate is conservative (2 characters per token, output tokens and a 16,000-character reserve subtracted), the budget and its source are recorded in the report, and the limitation is stated
errorCases.userImpact: A wrong window figure is visible in the report; accuracy is protected by dividing earlier, at the cost of more calls

errorCases.scenario: A typed answer failure is thrown from inside the free-form final emit
errorCases.detection: The free-form lookup catches HandlingBudgetError from the tool loop, as executePlan would otherwise turn any error that is not a ConnectionExecutionError into a failed lookup with no data
errorCases.response: It throws a LookupFailedError carrying the tool results as partial and the HandlingReport; failedOutput keeps both; the pipeline raises the answer-step failure with the report and does not attempt a second synthesis
errorCases.userImpact: The caller receives the failure with what the search found and how far the handling got

errorCases.scenario: A typed answer failure is thrown from inside synthesize
errorCases.detection: The driver's catch sees HandlingBudgetError or ShaperAnswerStepFailedError
errorCases.response: The driver passes it through unchanged instead of mapping it to 'answer-invalid', and the step tool returns it as StepOutputError with the declared code and its data
errorCases.userImpact: The caller receives the error with the lookup results and the report

errorCases.scenario: A stored handling value is malformed
errorCases.detection: parseHandling finds a missing required field or a wrong type, as for the stored {}
errorCases.response: The value is treated as absent by mergeHandling, renderReportHead and isAnswerReport; it is not written back
errorCases.userImpact: An old record is read without handling instead of failing

errorCases.scenario: The aggregate of a nested plan reports uncovered parts
errorCases.detection: collectPlanSources reads parseHandling(metadata.handling) of that plan's aggregate task and finds a non-empty notCovered
errorCases.response: One source per uncovered part is added, named by the aggregate task's path and the part id, so the run is incomplete
errorCases.userImpact: A partly failed aggregation never produces a run labelled complete

migration.stateBefore: synthesize and runAggregator render the whole of their inputs into one prompt and make one model call with no size check (src/analyze/context/synthesizer.ts:117-169, src/analyze/runtimes/shared/aggregator.ts:100-155). finalizeSynthesize(raw, execution?) is called by the bundle handler with the execution (src/analyze/context/synthesizer.ts:191-225, src/daemon/steps/analyze-step/phases/bundle.ts:90). The free-form lookup's final emit takes the whole conversation, a non-ConnectionExecutionError from it becomes a failed lookup that keeps data only for a LookupFailedError, and the short-circuit copies only the seven layers (src/analyze/explore/freeform-probe.ts:150-200, src/analyze/explore/executor.ts:690-715, src/analyze/context/driver.ts:1004-1044, 1662-1690). AnswerReport.handling is typed unknown (src/analyze/completeness.ts:206), mergeAnswerReports is binary with a prefix, renderReportHead shows no handling (src/analyze/completeness.ts:377-420), and collectPlanSources skips each plan's aggregate task (src/analyze/executor/plan-sources.ts:43-92). The step tool keeps no progress on a bad reply.
migration.stateAfter: The four callers use one shared helper that divides when the HLD's table says so or the rendered input does not fit a conservative budget measured before every attempt. Evidence and findings are assembled in code, a staged combine writes only the summary and always ends, a failed part or combine is named while the other results are kept. finalizeSynthesize keeps execution in second place and takes progress third. A typed failure from the free-form final emit survives the executor with its data and the handling, the handling reaches the delivered answer on every path through the report, and renderReportHead shows it. The step tool carries an AnswerProgress object persisted on every transition.

Move the free-form final emit onto the helper, add the handling callback and field, carry handling in LookupFailedError and failedOutput, and copy it in extractSoleFreeformResult onto the derived report

migration.backwardCompat: All new state and report fields are optional or additive, and the one addition to an existing union value (partitionedBy 'mixed') is on a contract this Story owns. finalizeSynthesize keeps raw and execution in their positions and returns the bundle exactly as before when no progress is given, so the bundle handler's existing call is unchanged. A step state written before the change lacks the progress and is read as a single-pass state. A stored bundle with an open handling object stays valid and a malformed value is read as absent. A report without handling renders the same head. A small request whose input fits makes the same calls as before. synthesize, runAggregator, runFinalStructuredEmit, mergeAnswerReports, collectPlanSources, concludeRun and renderReportHead keep their signatures with new parameters optional. The registered MCP bundle argument is unchanged and the legacy emit_bundle turn is kept.

alternativesConsidered.name: Size table plus a rendered-input fit check in one shared helper, with caller adapters, carried-data failures and a rendered handling line
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: One helper divides an answer-writing call's input when either the HLD's size table says the request is above the partition size or the rendered input does not fit a conservative character budget, and it carries the handling report to the delivered answer on every path.
alternativesConsidered.approach: (1) Decision: the helper partitions when EITHER condition holds: the measured size (sc3) is at or above the table's partition size, or the single rendered input (messages, repeated context, absent-input section) exceeds the budget. The table maps XS and S to single pass, and M, L and XL to parts; the fit check forces division of anything that does not fit regardless of size, and it is measured before every provider attempt, including each schema-repair retry with its actual repair note (the note is capped at 8,000 characters of listed errors, the rest summarised as a count), and a retry whose input would not fit divides the part further. (2) Budget: provider.inputBudgetChars when declared; else for a local model (window tokens minus output tokens) times 2 characters per token, stated as a conservative estimate and not a bound; else 60,000 characters; a reserve of 16,000 characters for framing, schema text and the first repair note. The report records the budget and its source, and the wording never claims truncation is prevented. (3) Division and assembly as before: blocks by directory then file, one oversize block in consecutive sections of at least 4,000 characters, ordinals separate from keys, part replies capped at 2,000 characters of summary, evidence and findings assembled in code by ordinal, a staged combine of N summaries into ceil(N/g) with g at least 2 that writes only the summary layers, a combine failure returning the per-part results with the failure reported, a typed budget error carrying the results and the report when nothing can fit. (4) Callers: synthesize, runAggregator, the free-form final emit and the step tool. The free-form final emit reports its HandlingReport through a handling callback on the tool loop's arguments and a handling field on the loop's result and on the free-form lookup output; a HandlingBudgetError from it is turned by the free-form lookup into a LookupFailedError that carries the tool results as partial and the HandlingReport, so the executor keeps them and the pipeline reports the answer-step failure with the report. The short-circuit copies the handling into the report that reportFromLookups derives. finalizeSynthesize keeps its execution parameter and gains progress after it. (5) Reporting: mergeHandling composes a merged report by fixed rules, collectPlanSources reads each plan's aggregate handling, and renderReportHead renders a handling line on both paths. (6) Step tool: an AnswerProgress object, emit_part and emit_combine outputs that reuse the registered bundle argument, persisted on every transition.
pros: Keeps the HLD's stated table and adds the fit check, so no input is sent that does not fit, whatever its measured size
Accuracy first: more parts and calls are accepted wherever either condition says so
One code path for all four callers
Every route by which the handling report and a failure reach the delivered answer is stated
cons: Largest alternative: touches the synthesizer, aggregator, free-form lookup and loop, executor failure carrying, plan-sources, completeness rendering, step tool state and wire
The 2 characters per token ratio, the 60,000 default, the 16,000 reserve and the 2,000 cap are chosen constants

alternativesConsidered.name: Size table only, separate implementations per path
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Decide only from the five sizes with a fixed table and implement division and combine once for the lookup pipeline and once for the aggregator.
alternativesConsidered.approach: Define a table from size to single pass or partitioned with fixed part counts, and implement the division and combine separately for synthesize and for runAggregator. The size class decides; there is no check that a call fits.
pros: Follows the HLD wording of a stated table literally
Each path can be tuned independently
cons: A size class counts files and items, not characters, so a medium request with large items can still overflow a call
Two implementations that can drift apart
Fixed part counts do not follow the model in use
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Literal to the HLD but a size class does not bound characters, so an input can still overflow a call.

alternativesConsidered.name: Smallest: halve and retry when the provider refuses the input
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Keep one pass as today and only when the provider refuses the input as too large split it in half, retry and combine the halves.
alternativesConsidered.approach: Catch the provider's size refusal in synthesize and runAggregator, split the input at a file boundary into two halves, run each and combine, repeating on refusal. No table, no budget, no step tool part turn beyond a retry.
cons: Only the CLI provider refuses; a local model truncates silently, so input is lost with no signal, which defeats accuracy
The sizes in a refusal may be absent so the split point is a guess
No section rule for one large item and no handling report, so ac3 and ac6 are not met by design
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: A local model truncates silently instead of refusing, so input is lost with no signal; this violates k1, k2 and k3.

sequenceDefinition.narrative: How a step-tool answer is handled in parts: the helper decides, the client replies per part, progress is persisted on every transition, and the combine ends with either the assembled answer or the per-part fallback.

participants.label: In-session model
participants.description: Emits part and combine replies through the registered bundle argument.

participants.label: Step handler
participants.description: Validates each reply and persists the progress by re-encoding the state token.

participants.label: Handling helper
participants.description: Measures the rendered input, divides the evidence, assembles output in code.

messages.label: prepareSynthesize(args, progress)
messages.description: Asks for the next turn: answer, part or combine.

messages.label: turn within budget
messages.description: The rendered input of the turn fits the budget.

messages.label: emit_part / emit_combine
messages.description: The prompt, user turn and schema of the turn, with the new state token.

messages.label: bundle reply
messages.description: A seven-layer reply for the part, or system, focus and summary for a combine.

messages.label: finalizeSynthesize(reply, execution, progress)
messages.description: A bad reply increments retries; at the bound the part or the combine is recorded as failed.

messages.label: next progress or final bundle
messages.description: Evidence and findings are assembled in code; a combine failure returns the per-part results.
